newsitem.title: UK: Allied sets up taskforce to study merger.
newsitem.headline: Allied sets up taskforce to study merger.

text.p: Drinks to pub group Allied Domecq has set up a taskforce to study whether a planned merger between rivals Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness gives them an unfair dominance in any of its markets, said chairman Sir Christopher Hogg.
"We have set up a taskforce to look at the issue," said Hogg in an interview on Tuesday.
It was far too early to say whether Allied would complain to monopoly authorities about the planned merger, said Hogg, "there is so much to be examined and analysed."
"We have to look at it on a market by market, territory by territory basis. But we have a duty to complain if its in shareholders interests," he said.
Spain and the United States are expected to be the most sensitive markets for Allied. In the U.S. GrandMet is the largest spirits company and Guinness the largest whisky group.
Spain is Allied's largest European market, the group sold some 2 million cases of Ballantine's whisky there last year and half a million cases of Beefeater gin.

Spain and the United States together generate half of Allied's profits in its spirits and wine division. In Spain GrandMet owned J&B is the largest Scotch brand and Guinness sells Johnnie Walker whisky and Gordon's gin in the region.

Earlier Hogg told reporters however that he did not want the companies "response to be one of complaint," and he talked in positive terms about consolidation in the industry as a force for improving growth.
"Spirits is a tough industry in which to get growth and any thing which is likely to improve growth is going to be looked at seriously," he told reporters.
"Consolidation does afford opportunities to grow profits whether from increased marketing power or reduced costs."
"Consolidation is one way forward for the industry," he said.

If Allied had demerged its spirits division, as some shareholders called for a year ago, it would have meant a 15 month programme and a good deal of turmoil, leaving it less able to take advantage of any fall out from the GrandMet/Guinness merger, said Hogg.

"I think we are in a very good position following yesterday's merger, we have 12 of the top 100 brands, we are in increasingly good shape in wines and spirits and we can seize opportunities open to us which will be greatly increased by the merger," said Hogg.
